objective: Make Pi perform proportional, context-aware, evidence-backed software engineering using one authoritative initiative and one canonical work graph.

bootstrap.approval: User approved the discovery architecture and all four recommendations, accepted phased delivery, and authorized bootstrap in this conversation.

constraints: Exactly one authoritative planning JSON per initiative
Preserve historical workflows and migration evidence
No fabricated verification or retroactive TDD

acceptanceCriteria.text: One validated initiative survives interruption and resumption without duplicate task authority or silent lost updates.
Applicable practices have reasons and derive concrete obligations linked to work and acceptance criteria; irrelevant ceremony is omitted.
A one-task bug flow records meaningful RED/GREEN evidence and cannot complete with missing, failed, stale, aborted, or fabricated verification.
The TODO docket is a projection of SWE work and all mutations use the same service and completion gates.
Plans support bounded hierarchy, dependencies, intentional revision, artifact references, and bounded fresh context across sessions.
Legacy work is never silently activated or presented as freshly verified; package checks and supported behavior tests pass.

assessment.reason: Cross-extension redesign involving durable state, verification trust, compatibility, and context; delivered through small independent increments.
unknowns: Relevant source snapshot bounds and newly created-file handling need a tested MVP contract.
Historical release and test dependencies must be inventoried before retirement.

practices.reason: Reducers, persistence, evidence gates, and projections have deterministic test seams.
Interruption and concurrent sessions must not corrupt or silently overwrite authority.
Paths, permission-preserving execution, evidence provenance, and human-only waivers are trust boundaries.
Retire duplicate authority and dangling imports without restoring obsolete orchestration.
Reuse keyboard-friendly UI and prevent repeated full-plan injection.

obligations.text: Characterize the post-deletion baseline; document every obsolete expectation retired and preserve unrelated behavior.
Test closed schemas, graph/reference invariants, readiness, coverage, and legal transitions, including invalid inputs.
Prove atomic persistence, stale revision rejection, cross-process exclusion, cancellation, and interruption recovery.
Verification observes real outcomes without bypassing command permissions; missing/stale/failed/aborted evidence and model-forged human waivers cannot complete work.
Run a one-task RED → fix → GREEN → review → complete flow and reload its durable state; label fixture versus live observations honestly.
Docket/command/tool views share authority; finish cannot bypass SWE gates; SWE loads without pi-todo; legacy completion remains historical.
Test bounded context, completed-task collapse, preservation of other extensions' context, and no initiative rewind on session branching.
Validate safe artifact paths/hashes and schema identity; support attachments only with explicit layout validation and do not mutate historical workflows.
Preserve keyboard navigation, bounded rendering, and useful non-TUI output.
Run npm run typecheck, npm run check, npm run check:commands, and npm test; explain any remaining failures rather than declaring qualification complete.

evidence.summary: Model self-review (not independent or human approval): no blocking findings. The retirement report clearly separates historical fixtures from active runtime authority; pi-todo uses only the optional shared lifecycle probe, preserves fail-closed mutation behavior when that probe rejects, and exposes no deleted SWE storage/workflow coupling. Qualification and package-resource assertions exclude the legacy runtime and retired orchestration skill while retaining the thin todo surface.

Model self-review (not independent or human approval): blocking evidence-integrity/correctness finding. SweService associates completed verification evidence with mutable #selected rather than the initiative captured by prepareVerification. Any intervening status/next/prepare call for another initiative can change #selected, causing observeToolResult to append evidence to the wrong initiative (or attempt to), while the collector evidence carries no initiative identity. Existing tests cover one initiative and therefore do not exercise this interleaving. Ordinary-bash permission provenance, persisted-evidence restart completion, source freshness, and explicit pi-model-self-review labeling otherwise appear sound in the reviewed scope.

Model self-review (not independent or human approval): no blocking findings remain. Prepared verification is bound to its initiative independently of mutable selection; exact ordinary bash tool-call/result observation preserves the permission boundary; completion checks outcome, contract fingerprint, source freshness, and RED-before-GREEN; persisted evidence supports completion after restart; review provenance is explicitly pi-model-self-review; runtime coverage verifies selection changes cannot cross-attribute evidence.

decisions.text: Use phased implementation and a new foundation initiative; do not revive historical rollout authority.
Retire standalone engineering TODO writes; preserve legacy inspection/import.
Automatically create minimal initiatives for implementation, not discussion.
Enforce mutation/completion integrity, not blanket coding-tool interception.
Waivers of already-required obligations require explicit human approval.
Collect verification by observing exact ordinary bash tool calls; never execute checks through internal pi.exec.
decisions.basis: Pinned Pi and installed permission-system API inspection plus negative integration tests

decisions.text: Completion follows each obligation’s explicit evidence kinds; semantic review is runtime-recorded model self-review, and RED/GREEN obligations require an observed failed command before the passing command.
decisions.basis: Approved design requires distinctly labeled LLM review, code-enforced observation order, and no claim of independent review.

risks.text: Restoring obsolete tests/APIs can accidentally recreate the removed orchestration engine.
risks.mitigation: Characterize and retire expectations explicitly; keep the slice small.

risks.text: Internal command execution may bypass installed bash permissions.
risks.mitigation: Inspect permission integration and prove equivalent enforcement before exposing verification execution.

risks.text: Concurrent writers or changed tests/config may make passing evidence stale.
risks.mitigation: Atomic mutation, cross-process tests, contract/source freshness checks.

risks.text: Schema and context grow into process overhead.
risks.mitigation: One-task fixtures, bounded projections, no mandatory hierarchy or exhaustive checklist.
